To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Specifically, I request a structured dataset or database export (such as a CSV, Excel, or similar machine-readable file) containing the following fields for each traffic stop
1. Unique Identifier: Any incident number, case number, CAD event number, or unique stop ID associated with the record.
2. Date: The date the traffic stop occurred.
3. Time: The time the traffic stop was initiated (and cleared, if maintained).
4. Agency: The initiating or reporting agency/division.
5. Problem Description: The initial call/incident nature and any updated problem description or disposition noting a deviation from a standard traffic stop.
6. Responding Unit: The unit identifier(s) or badge/car number(s) assigned to or responding to the stop.
7. Location: The street address, intersection, or block-level location of the stop. (Note: If exact location details raise specific statutory privacy or safety exemptions, providing the corresponding police district, beat, or sector is an acceptable alternative.)
8. Reason for the Stop: The statutory violation code cited, infraction/offense code, or the generalized stop category recorded by the officer or dispatch system.

I also request that, if possible and pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(d), fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest and not made for commercial gain. The requested documents will be made available to the public at MuckRock.com.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brent Skalling

title: RMS/CAD Data Sharing with LexisNexis (Northfield & St. Louis Park Police)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) Screenshot, document, or report that shows all agencies with active LexisNexis integrations. 

2) A screenshot, document, report, or comment that explains how Northfield PD and St. Louis Park PD's data is being shared with LexisNexis. (this may be the same responsive document as item 1). 

Context: We asked Northfield PD about how their data is making its way to LexisNexis. They pointed us to Rice & Steele 911, who said they do not manage any RMS system, and that they use CentralSquare for their CAD. They also said there is no integration with LexisNexis on their end. I'm sure there's a simple answer, but I'm trying to unravel the mystery of how Northfield PD's data is showing up on the Community Crime Map - and neither Northfield or Rice & Steele 911 appear to know. Are you able to shed light on this? We did see slides relating to the Police Executive Steering Committee for July 21, 2026 which included a list of agencies still contributing data to LexisNexis. St. Louis Park PD was not on this list, despite having a connection with LexisNexis. Shortly after July 21, SLPPD confirmed they use LOGIS, and their data has been appearing on CommunityCrimeMap.com for a while. Are you able to help me understand why they were not on that list, while others were? 

Sorry for the back to back requests - I tried to go right to the agencies but they're stumped. Thanks for the help with this.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal
